glossary.m: the big lesson a story teaches, said as a full sentence
what a story is about, in a word or two, like loyalty or winter
the words characters say out loud in a story
the marks “ and ” that go around the exact words someone says
the part that tells who is talking, like said Lucy
the main part of a word that holds its meaning, like ject, which means throw
a part added to the front or the end of a word, like un- or -ed
telling the truth, even when it is hard

cards.title: World Notes: A Lion’s Mane
cards.sub: A real thing behind the story
cards.todo: Read the note. Then read the chapter with your lens in mind.
text: Only grown male lions have a mane, the thick ring of hair around the head and neck.
A big mane makes a lion look larger. Scientists think a darker, fuller mane can also show other lions that he is strong and healthy.
A mane takes years to grow. In the story, Aslan’s golden mane is part of what makes him look so royal.

transcripts.welcome: Hi, it's Opti. Look back at the whole book so far. Pick your strongest proof, and finish your response on theme.
transcripts.guide1: Word work: roll ject words, fix a passage in passes, and roll long words.
transcripts.guide2: Look back at Chapters 13 to 15 for your best details.
transcripts.guide3: Today you finish your literary response.

notes.wordParts: The root ject means throw. reject = throw back. inject = throw into. eject = throw out. project = throw forward.
notes.grammar: Quotation marks go around the exact words someone says. The first word gets a capital. The comma or period goes inside the closing mark: “Let him approach,” said Aslan.
notes.spelling: A long word is often a root with parts added. Find the root first: un + expect + ed = unexpected.
notes.wgrd: A theme needs proof from the beginning, the middle and the end. Edmund betrays his family, he is forgiven, and Aslan gives his life for him.
vocab: someone who betrays the trust of their own side
to make up for a wrong you have done
giving up something precious for something or someone more important
coming back to life after death

plate.alt: A painting of a lion's head with a thick golden-brown mane, looking straight out of the picture
plate.credit: Portrait of a Lion · Rosa Bonheur, 1879 · Museo del Prado, Madrid · Public domain
plate.look: A painting by Rosa Bonheur, a French painter, from 1879. She studied real animals up close so she could paint them true to life. Look at the thick mane and the calm, steady eyes. In the story, Aslan is a great lion, and the children feel both glad and serious when they look at him.
plate.lookBtn: Tap to learn about this painting of a lion

Say what the word part means. Then tap Roll the Dice. Say what the word means, and tap Check My Thinking. Roll all six words.

mods.todo: Choose one word. Write one sentence about the theme.
mods.script: One word can carry a big idea. Traitor. At first, Edmund acts like a traitor, but in Chapter 13 his family forgives him. One word, one big idea. Now choose your word, and write your own sentence about the theme.

mods.todo: Fix it in passes. Then tap every word that needs fixing.
mods.script: Two passes, like an editor. its snowing, said peter. Pass one, capitals: It's and Peter. Pass two, apostrophes: it's means it is. The comma is already inside. Now do your passes, and tap every word that needs fixing.

mods.todo: Roll the dice. Name the root and the parts. Then check.
mods.script: Dice roll: uncovered! Cover the front and the end. What's left? Cover! That's the root, and the parts are un and e d. Tap Roll the dice, say the root and the parts, and tap Check my answer.

virtue.title: Truth Watch: Is someone being honest?

items.t: Mr. Beaver says the Witch is not really the Queen of Narnia.
items.why: He tells the truth about her, even in front of her messenger.

items.t: The Witch’s messenger calls her “the Queen of Narnia.”
items.why: That title is not really hers.

items.t: Aslan keeps his promise to the Witch, even though it costs him so much.
items.why: He does exactly what he said he would do.
